text:
[IRET.8.4] **`logical: false` overlay — the retraction path.**
`terminal_left_retract` is the engine function that runs when a rule's
supporting token is retracted. Normally it:

1. Copies TMS IDs to a local stack array (re-entrancy safety).
2. Withdraws from the TMS to retrieve the logical fact IDs.
3. For each ID, retracts the WM fact — potentially triggering further
   alpha/beta retractions (cascade).
4. Frees the scratch buffer if `caller_must_free`.

Under `logical: false`, steps 1–4 are absent. `terminal_left_retract` only
removes the terminal token from the token pool. No WM retraction is
triggered from the TMS path.

This is the mechanism by which [LNOG.4.2]'s no-cascade guarantee
holds: the observable consequence — a
supporting token's retraction withdraws nothing else — stays in
[LNOG.4.2]; the named steps of this engine's function are
implementation.

idris.name: Iret_8_4__explicit_only
idris.note: A program emitting into no `logical` schema -- every `logical: false` program by [LNOG.3.2], and every witness the core proofs run.

idris.name: iret_11_4__step_agrees
idris.note: On such a program the engine with truth maintenance takes exactly the core engine's step with an empty table: the retraction path withdraws nothing else, which is [LNOG.4.2]'s guarantee on the model.
